tool_summary: Copies files while setting ownership, permissions, and directory structure in one step, commonly used in build/deploy scripts (make install targets) to place binaries into system directories.
platform_notes: Core flag semantics (-m, -o, -g, -d) are consistent between GNU and BSD install.

rules.description: The -m/--mode flag with a setuid or setgid bit (e.g. 4755, 2755) creates a binary that executes with the file owner's or group's privileges regardless of who runs it. This is a classic privilege escalation vector if the owner is root.

Installing to a system binary directory (/usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, /bin, /sbin) places a new executable somewhere it may be picked up by other users' PATH or by privileged processes, typically requiring root and silently overwriting any existing file of the same name.
rules.reversible_note: Any existing file at the destination is overwritten without confirmation.

rules.description: Copies a file, setting ownership/permissions/directory structure in one step.
rules.reversible_note: If the destination already existed, its prior contents are overwritten and not recoverable by install itself.
